title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE FRAMEWORK ACT ON MILITARY WELFARE
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE FRAMEWORK ACT ON MILITARY WELFARE

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Framework Act on Military Welfare and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Formulation and Implementation of Master Plans for Military Welfare, etc.)
(1) The Minister of National Defense shall prepare a master plan for military welfare under Article 6 (1) of the Framework Act on Military Welfare (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as a "master plan") by the end of June of the year preceding the first year of the master plan and, after consulting with the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies, report it to the President by the end of December of the same year.
(2) The heads of the relevant central administrative agencies shall notify the Minister of National Defense of their annual implementation plans for the fields under their jurisdiction by the end of January each year and of the results of implementing those plans by the end of January of the following year, respectively.
(3) The Minister of National Defense and the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies may request central administrative agencies and other relevant institutions and organizations to submit materials necessary for the formulation and implementation of master plans or annual implementation plans and the promotion of military welfare projects, etc. In such cases, central administrative agencies and other relevant institutions and organizations shall cooperate unless there are special circumstances.

Article 3 (Methods of Surveys on the Actual State of Military Welfare, etc.)
(1) A survey on the actual state of military welfare under Article 7 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "survey") shall include the following matters:
1. Economic circumstances, including income, expenditure, and assets;
2. Family relationships, including marriage, childbirth, child-rearing, support of dependents, and the composition of cohabiting families;
3. Lifestyles, including consumption and leisure;
4. Educational conditions for children;
5. Housing, including the use of military housing and homeownership;
6. The actual state of medical support, including conditions at military medical institutions;
7. The distribution and degree of use of welfare facilities and sports facilities (hereinafter referred to as "welfare facilities, etc.") and welfare needs;
8. Other matters concerning military welfare deemed necessary by the Minister of National Defense.
(2) Where an additional survey becomes necessary due to changes in the social environment relating to military service and military welfare, etc., the Minister of National Defense may supplement the survey under paragraph (1) by conducting an ad hoc survey.

Article 4 (Composition of Military Welfare Committee)
(1) "Public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Civil Service of the relevant central administrative agencies" in Article 8 (3) of the Act means senior public officials belonging to the following ministries or agencies who are in charge of affairs relating to the promotion of military welfare: <Amended on December 31, 2008; March 15, 2010; March 23, 2013; October 1, 2025; December 30, 2025>
1. Ministry of Health and Welfare;
2. Ministry of Gender Equality and Family;
3. Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport;
4. Ministry of Planning and Budget;
5. Other relevant central administrative agencies deemed necessary by the Minister of National Defense in relation to military welfare.
(2) Where persons with extensive knowledge and experience in military welfare are commissioned as members of the Military Welfare Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") pursuant to Article 8 (3) of the Act, the number of such members shall not exceed three.
(3) The terms of office of members under paragraph (1) shall be the periods during which they hold their respective positions, and the terms of office of members commissioned pursuant to paragraph (2) shall be two years. In such cases, members under paragraph (2) may be recommissioned for only one further term.

Article 4-2 (Dismissal of Members)
The Minister of National Defense may dismiss a member commissioned pursuant to Article 8 (3) of the Act where the member falls under any of the following:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform duties due to a mental or physical disability;
2. Where the member has committed misconduct in connection with duties;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable as a member due to neglect of duties, impairment of dignity, or any other reason;
4. Where the member personally expresses that it is difficult to perform duties.

Article 5 (Operation of Committee)
(1) The Chairperson of the Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Chairperson") shall represent the Committee and exercise overall control over its affairs.
(2) Where the Chairperson is unable to perform duties due to an unavoidable reason, a member designated in advance by the Chairperson shall act on the Chairperson's behalf.
(3) The Chairperson shall convene and preside over meetings of the Committee.
(4) Where the Chairperson intends to convene the Committee, the Chairperson shall determine the date, time, and place of the meeting and the agenda for deliberation and notify each member thereof in writing at least seven days before the meeting. Provided, That this shall not apply where there is an urgent reason.
(5) A majority of the incumbent members of the Committee, including the Chairperson, shall constitute a quorum for a meeting, and resolutions shall be passed with the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(6) Where deemed necessary for the performance of its duties, the Committee may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, research institutions, organizations, etc. to submit materials or opinions, etc., and may have relevant public officials or experts attend its meetings to hear their opinions.
(7) Allowances and travel expenses may be paid, within budgetary limits, to members, experts, etc. attending meetings of the Committee. Provided, That this shall not apply where a member who is a public official or a relevant public official attends a meeting in direct connection with the affairs under that official's jurisdiction.
(8) Except as provided in this Decree, matters necessary for the operation of the Committee shall be determined by the Chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 6 (Welfare Committees for Each Branch of the Armed Forces)
A welfare committee may be established for each branch of the armed forces, as prescribed by the Minister of National Defense, to deliberate on matters concerning the formulation and implementation of welfare policies for that branch and to have the Chairperson propose related matters to the Committee.

Article 6-2 (Criteria for Designation of Entrusted Institutions, etc.)
(1) The criteria for designation of an institution entrusted with duties concerning the management of military housing under Article 9-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "institution entrusted with military housing management") shall be as follows:
1. It shall have personnel with expertise in housing management, such as housing managers;
2. It shall have facilities and equipment, such as computerized systems for housing management;
3. It shall have the financial capacity necessary to perform duties concerning the management of military housing;
4. It shall ensure the security, safety, etc. necessary for the management of military housing.
(2) Where the Minister of National Defense intends to designate an institution entrusted with military housing management, the Minister shall give advance public notice of the designation plan, schedule, designation criteria, etc. on the website of the Ministry of National Defense.
(3) An institution, corporation, or organization seeking designation as an institution entrusted with military housing management shall submit to the Minister of National Defense an application for designation prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of National Defense (including an application in electronic form), accompanied by the following documents (including electronic documents):
1. Documents prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of National Defense as documents proving that the designation criteria under each subparagraph of paragraph (1) have been met;
2. A record of projects carried out in the field of housing management (only where such a record exists).
(4) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (3), the Minister of National Defense shall review whether all the designation criteria under each subparagraph of paragraph (1) have been met and decide whether to grant designation.
(5) When deciding whether to grant designation under paragraph (4), the Minister of National Defense may take into account the record of projects carried out in the field of housing management.
(6) The Minister of National Defense may designate multiple institutions entrusted with military housing management for the management of military housing by region.
(7) Where the Minister of National Defense designates an institution entrusted with military housing management, the Minister shall give public notice of the details in the Official Gazette.
(8) Where an institution entrusted with military housing management falls under Article 9-2 (2) 2 or 3 of the Act, the Minister of National Defense may set a period not exceeding three months and require the institution to rectify the violations, taking into account the motives for, details of, and seriousness of the violations, etc. In such cases, if rectification within the rectification period is difficult due to a natural disaster or other unavoidable reason, or if the Minister deems it necessary in view of the extent of harm to the management of military housing, etc., the Minister may extend the rectification period once by up to three months. <Newly Inserted on July 16, 2024>
(9) Where an institution entrusted with military housing management fails to rectify the violations within the rectification period under paragraph (8), the Minister of National Defense shall revoke the entrustment under Article 9-2 of the Act. <Newly Inserted on July 16, 2024>
(10) Matters necessary for the detailed particulars of the criteria and procedures for designation of institutions entrusted with military housing management, the operation of such institutions, revocation of entrustment, etc., other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (9), shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of National Defense. <Amended on July 16, 2024>

Article 7 (Eligibility Criteria for Occupants of Housing Supplied on a Priority Basis, etc.)
(1) The Minister of National Defense may secure the number of housing units, etc. to be supplied on a priority basis under Article 10 (1) of the Act through consultation with the project entity constructing the relevant housing, within the scope of special housing supply for military personnel prescribed by statutes and regulations concerning housing supply, and then supply such housing on a priority basis to military personnel who are heads of households that do not own a home.
(2) Occupants of housing supplied under paragraph (1) shall be selected in descending order of scores awarded for the following evaluation factors; where scores are equal, priority shall be given to the person who has not owned a home for a longer period: <Amended on August 11, 2016>
1. Length of time without home ownership;
2. Length of military service;
3. Number of dependent family members;
4. Period of enrollment in housing subscription savings under Article 56 of the Housing Act;
5. Whether the applicant supports a family member with a disability;
6. Whether the applicant supports a lineal ascendant aged 65 or older (including a lineal ascendant of the applicant's spouse), etc.
(3) The evaluation factors under each subparagraph of paragraph (2) shall be evaluated on a scale totaling 100 points, and the combined score for the length of time without home ownership and the length of military service shall account for at least 50 percent of the total score. Other details, including the specific allocation of evaluation points and the proportions of points assigned to the length of time without home ownership and the length of military service, shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense.
(4) In selecting occupants of housing supplied to military personnel who do not own a home by a corporation established for the purpose of promoting the stability of the livelihoods and the welfare of military personnel, after the corporation has been supplied with housing sites under Article 10 (2) of the Act or purchased general property under paragraph (3) of that Article, and in handling related matters, scores shall be calculated taking into account factors such as the length of time without home ownership, length of military service, and whether the applicant supports a family member with a disability, and housing shall be allocated in descending order of scores. Specific matters, including the allocation of points and supply procedures, shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense. <Amended on July 7, 2025>
(5) Military personnel seeking to apply for housing supply to a project entity under Article 10 (4) of the Act shall, as prescribed by the Minister of National Defense, submit to the relevant project entity an application for housing supply (including an electronic document) after public notice inviting applications for occupancy, accompanied by documents concerning the calculation of scores for the selection of occupants under paragraph (4) (including electronic documents): Provided, That the project entity may have the accompanying documents submitted before the supply contract is concluded instead of at the time of the application for housing supply. <Newly Inserted on July 7, 2025>
(6) Where unavoidable for the performance of duties concerning the priority supply of housing, etc. under Article 10 of the Act, the Minister of National Defense may process data containing resident registration numbers under Article 19, subparagraph 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act. <Newly Inserted on January 16, 2013; July 7, 2025>

Article 7-2 (Establishment and Operation of a Sales Price Review Committee, etc.)
(1) The Minister of National Defense shall establish and operate a Sales Price Review Committee to deliberate on matters concerning Article 57 of the Housing Act, which applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 10-2 (1) of the Act. In such cases, the Sales Price Review Committee shall be established within 20 days from the date on which an application for approval of a project plan under Article 15 of the Housing Act is filed.
(2) Where a project entity under Article 10 (4) of the Act applies to the competent approval authority for approval of a project plan referred to in the latter sentence of paragraph (1), it shall immediately notify the Minister of National Defense of that fact.
(3) In granting approval for the recruitment of occupants pursuant to Article 10 (4) of the Act, the Minister of National Defense shall determine whether to grant approval based on the results of the review by the Sales Price Review Committee under paragraph (1).
(4) Articles 63 through 70 of the Enforcement Decree of the Housing Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the composition and operation of the Sales Price Review Committee under paragraph (1). In such cases, each reference to the "Committee" shall be deemed to mean the "Sales Price Review Committee", and each reference to the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu" shall be deemed to mean the "Minister of National Defense"; "calculation of basic-type construction costs for each Si/Gun/Gu" in subparagraph 2 of Article 63 of the Enforcement Decree of the Housing Act shall be deemed to mean "calculation of basic-type construction costs"; and each reference to "the relevant Si/Gun/Gu" in the proviso to Article 64 (2) 1 and Article 65 (6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Housing Act shall be deemed to mean the "Ministry of National Defense".

Article 7-3 (Restriction on Eligibility to Occupy Housing)
(1) The period of restriction on eligibility to occupy housing under Article 64 (7) of the Housing Act, which applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 10-2 (2) of the Act, shall extend from the date on which an act violating paragraph (1) or (6) of that Article is detected until 10 years thereafter.
(2) An administrative agency that detects an act violating Article 64 (1) or (6) of the Housing Act, which applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 10-2 (2) of the Act, shall notify the Minister of National Defense and the agency handling subscription applications for the relevant housing of the list of persons concerned without delay.
(3) The Minister of National Defense and the agency handling subscription applications for the relevant housing that receive notification under paragraph (2) shall manage the notified list in computerized form.

Article 7-4 (Imposition of Administrative Fines) Administrative fines under Article 106 (4) of the Housing Act, which applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 10-2 (4) of the Act, shall be imposed by the Minister of National Defense. In such cases, subparagraph 1 and items (v) and (w) of subparagraph 2 of Attached Table 5 to the Enforcement Decree of the Housing Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the criteria for their imposition.

Article 7-5 (Matters Necessary for Restrictions on Housing Sales Prices, etc.) Details necessary for restrictions on housing sales prices, etc., other than those prescribed in Articles 7-2 through 7-4, shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense in consultation with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 8 (Support for Education and Childcare for Children of Military Personnel)
(1) Where the Minister of National Defense or the Chief of Staff of any military service requests the transfer or admission of children of military personnel pursuant to Article 11 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Education shall support their transfer or admission, including the assignment of schools, in consultation with the competent office of education. <Amended 2008.12.31, 2013.3.23>
(2) The Minister of Education shall provide support to enable the establishment of national and public childcare centers in areas with a high concentration of military personnel, including areas of military official residences where military personnel and their families reside in connection with the performance of military duties. <Amended 2008.12.31, 2010.3.15, 2011.12.8, 2024.6.25>

Article 9 (Requirements for Admission to Board and Lodging Facilities, etc.)
(1) Residents of board and lodging facilities provided to children of military personnel pursuant to Article 11 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "dormitories for children of military personnel" in this Article) shall be selected in descending order of scores based on a combined assessment of the following factors, with a maximum total score of 100 points. In such cases, the score for the type of school, lifelong education facility, etc. attended shall account for at least 40 percent of the total score. <Amended 2015.3.17>
1. The type of school, lifelong education facility, etc. currently attended;
2. The length of service of military personnel who are lineal ascendants;
3. The duty locations of military personnel who are lineal ascendants;
4. Other criteria deemed necessary by the Minister of National Defense, including the ages of children of military personnel and the ranks of military personnel who are lineal ascendants.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), children of personnel dispatched overseas and children of persons supporting 3 or more children may be given priority for admission. <Amended 2015.3.17>
(3) Residents of dormitories for children of military personnel shall pay food expenses, utility charges, and other costs necessary for the maintenance and management of the dormitories, etc., as determined by the Minister of National Defense.
(4) Details concerning the management and operation, etc. of dormitories for children of military personnel shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 10 Deleted <2012.9.21>

Article 11 (Management and Operation of Welfare Facilities, etc.)
(1) The person responsible for the management of welfare facilities, etc. under Article 14 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "manager" in this Article) shall be designated from among officers of general or flag rank in each military service. <Amended 2017.9.5>
(2) A manager designated under paragraph (1) may, where necessary, delegate part of the duties concerning management of welfare facilities, etc. to military personnel or civilian employees of the military under the manager's authority.
(3) The designation of managers and partial delegation of duties to military personnel, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) may be effected instead by designating positions established in units at each level as positions responsible for performing the relevant duties.

Article 12 (Processing of Unique Identifying Information) Where unavoidable for the performance of the following duties, the Minister of National Defense may process data containing resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act:
1. Duties concerning support for military housing under Article 9 (1) of the Act;
2. Duties concerning the preferential supply of housing under Article 10 (1) of the Act.
